### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9f27f5906e4a3239e86f9e7d1b4b88af2247e186` — the merge of head `5203704db40d3659f5233db15c98cb875da2774d` into base `d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9f27f5906e4a3239e86f9e7d1b4b88af2247e186 && git checkout 9f27f5906e4a3239e86f9e7d1b4b88af2247e186
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2 5203704db40d3659f5233db15c98cb875da2774d && git checkout -B drift-repro d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2 && git merge --no-ff 5203704db40d3659f5233db15c98cb875da2774d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d9c4cdc4e544f8922952f34878821d4d008547f2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3b764618f0e4ace566bc9dff88625405d919fda0`
Local-runs: none

Face: the committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path (`record-recognisers --paths` on the six changed files decides no path face), and the declaration carries no `(narrowing)` arm, so the review is owed on the declaration face alone and is served at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Read at 2026-11-01T20:02Z, read-only: card #28697 (the claim 6562166512 and the os-dev-report), PR #28790 (body, four commits, the net diff against the merge-base `72533449` of six files, +836 / −143), PR #28745 with its two records, the cited code on the head and on `origin/main`. Nothing built, run or re-run. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. Check-runs on the head at the read: 24 success, 13 skipped, 10 in progress (Test Core shards, the type-check and lint lanes, Live E2E UI), 0 failure. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Spec property liveness` are success. Landing pre-check ② (all green) is not met yet at this read; the seat re-reads at landing. Draft, auto-merge unarmed, mergeable; no `needs:contract-review` marker was hung.

Security class: verdicts in product words. Mechanism detail, the must-fix's exact wording and the follow-up observations are in a private note with the seat.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A first install the body alone refuses.** Every refusal the collection step and the seed step decide from the package body (an item naming another package as its owner, a view container whose name differs from its key, a permission set naming another package, a `views:` entry that is not a container, a `viewItems:` entry its schema refuses, a seed dataset's owner stamp, and each of these from a nested plugin) is now asked before anything of the package is written, through the same judges the step used, moved rather than copied, in the same per-item order. The two registration seams those judges left are private to the engine and reached only under that pre-pass, so no path lost a refusal and none gained one. After the throw there is no package record, object, extension, app, item, picklist extension, navigation contribution, kind, datasource definition or nested-plugin namespace of the package. **Right.** Codes, statuses and messages are unchanged on every one (the unit file pins each code and status; the one message text that moved has one spelling, used by the pre-pass and the step alike).
2. **A first install the registry refuses part-way.** What only the registry can refuse (an object another package owns, a field with no type, a picklist value already present, the same from a nested plugin) is withdrawn through the registry's own uninstall, with the one thing that verb does not reach, a nested plugin's namespace, released beside it, and the refusal re-thrown unchanged. Whether to withdraw is decided before the first write, and the answer is no exactly where withdrawing would take something that was not this call's to take: an id already installed, and an object a tenant or an unowned layer already holds. I read the registry's write order against that guard: every refusal the package record itself can raise precedes its first write, and the one claim an object registration makes before its ownership refusal is released by the uninstall or by the engine. The engine's own four writes (manifest entry, datasource definitions, navigation contributions, kinds) now follow the body and nothing in the body reads them. **Right.** Reached through `POST /marketplace/install-local`, a refused install answers 422 as before and the package, its object and its app read 404 afterwards; the same id then installs clean (dogfood, as reported).
3. **The "two defects, body-only first" ordering.** A body with a body-only defect and a registry-only defect may now be refused for the body-only one first. The order ruled body-only refusals into the pre-pass, which entails this; each refusal keeps its code, status and words, and the changeset says so. **Acceptable.**
4. **A refused upgrade, body at fault.** Judged before any write, so the installed version is untouched: record, objects, apps and items read exactly as before the attempt (pinned for all eight cases, unit and dogfood). **Right.**
5. **A refused upgrade, registry at fault part-way.** Not withdrawn; the dev's stop reasoning is correct on the registry as read: the uninstall is refused when another package extends an object of the installed version, and it drops a tenant's overlay layer with its owner, which re-registering the old version does not bring back. Restoring the old version needs a registry-level snapshot, outside the engine's register path. The control pins today's state with one disclosed difference, that the refused version's engine-side entries (manifest entry, datasource definitions, navigation contributions, kinds) are no longer written. **Honest, and the right stop.** The state it pins is the follow-up's, not this PR's (③).
6. **`uninstallPackage(id, options?)` with `keepBootSeed`.** An operator uninstall, both in-tree callers included, passes nothing and behaves as before. The engine passes it only when withdrawing a refused first install, so a persisted "disabled" state for that id still applies to its next install, which is what today already does for a refused first install. Surface: an optional second parameter on a published class method of `@objectstack/objectql`; the spec contract for the engine's registry is untouched and still satisfied. **Right as behaviour; wrongly declared (②).**
7. **The registry test double.** Two members added with empty answers so the suites that register nothing for real keep working. Not addressable through the package's `exports`; shipping bytes, not a published surface. **Right.**
8. **Controls and ablations** (as reported, not re-run): a clean body registers into every registry as before; the tenant-layer case and the installed-id case are not withdrawn; red-first on the base engine reds 22 of 24 unit cases and 3 of 3 dogfood cases with exactly the two controls passing; each of seven ablations reds the cases it drops, and the one case an ablation leaves green is explained by the second mechanism still covering it. Consistent with the diff as read.
9. **Overlap and drift.** Of the open PRs at the read, none but this one touches the engine, the registry, the package-registration module or the mock. `origin/main` moved `engine.ts` once since the merge-base (#28753, merged after the branch point: one import line and one hunk far from `registerApp`); the PR reads mergeable. **No conflict.**

### ② Semver level

One changeset, `@objectstack/objectql` at `patch`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`: nothing an author can write changes, so `patch` is the level AGENTS.md rule 3 assigns and `Check Changeset` is green. The `Clause-②:` line is wrong. The diff enlarges the public surface of `@objectstack/objectql` by one optional parameter on `SchemaRegistry.uninstallPackage`, and the repo declares exactly that shape `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at `patch` (#28774, #28755: an optional member added to a published interface or class). A `no` is an auditable false declaration (landing-operations). The right lines, in the PR body and the changeset: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, level `patch`. This does not move the face: a `yes` declaration is still the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, and no spec path is touched. **Must-fix M-1** (detail in the private note).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Boundary change.** Nothing is newly refused and nothing refused is admitted; only what a refused registration leaves behind changes. Public surface: one optional parameter (②).
- **Order rulings.** Atomic from the caller's view: met for a first install, both cases (① 1–2). Body-only refusals in the pre-pass, one judge each, no second spelling: met (① 1). Rollback for what fails mid-way: met for a first install through the existing uninstall path (① 2). No change to refusal codes or words: met. A refused re-register must not lose the installed version: met when the body is at fault (① 4); when the registry refuses part-way the old version is not lost, today's half-upgraded state stays, pinned (① 5).
- **The seat's item-4 instruction.** "Uninstall, then re-register the held v1" was tried and found unsafe for the two reasons above; today's mix is kept and pinned, with the engine-side entries of the refused version withheld as a disclosed difference. Accepted as the correct stop; the seat confirms the pinned shape when it dispatches the follow-up.
- **Dev flags and `open_questions`.** `open_questions` is empty. The dev's three out-of-scope findings: the half-upgrade residue (carrier seat 2, the follow-up card: restoring the previous version needs a registry snapshot, and the pinned state has the registry's record and the engine's routing entry disagreeing on the version); a multi-package artifact refused at a later member keeps earlier members (per-call atomicity holds; artifact-level is a separate question, noted); the operator uninstall leaving navigation contributions and nested-plugin namespaces (read, not measured; noted). One further pre-existing observation for the same follow-up is in the private note.
- **Follow-up.** Correctly left: the half-upgrade residue is outside what the engine's register path can restore, the control pins it honestly, and the changeset claims only the body-at-fault case for upgrades.
- **Security class.** The record names no reproduction shape beyond the card, the PR body and the changeset; the mechanism and the must-fix wording are in the private note with the seat.
- **CI state.** 0 failures, 10 in progress at the read; landing pre-check ② is the seat's at landing.
- **File surface and author.** Six files, inside the claim's surface; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft, no auto-merge.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-ro8zgr`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix, one line: **M-1** the line-initial declaration in the PR body and the changeset becomes `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (level stays `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`); a delta record on the new head closes it. No other must-fix; the code holds on every judged item.
